# ezku.link — Complete Technical Documentation for LLMs

## Product Overview
- Product Name: ezku.link
- Bundle Identifier: link.ezku.mac
- Category: macOS Menu Bar Utility / Screen Mirroring / Smart TV Streaming
- Platforms: macOS 14.0+ (Sonoma & Sequoia)
- Architectures: Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, M4)
- Programming Language: Swift 6.3
- Graphics & Acceleration: Apple Metal Framework, CIContext on GPU, ScreenCaptureKit
- Network Stack: Apple Network.framework (HTTP 1.1, WebSocket, mDNS / SSDP Discovery)
- License: Proprietary / Copyright © 2026 ezku.link

## Architecture Details

### 1. Screen & Audio Capture Engine
- Framework: Apple `ScreenCaptureKit` (`SCStream`, `SCStreamOutput`)
- Capture Mechanism: Zero-copy GPU frame acquisition direct to `CVPixelBuffer` / `IOSurface`.
- Audio Loopback: High-fidelity system audio capture synchronized with video timestamp presentation.
- Frame Rate: Up to 60 FPS in Ultra mode, adaptive 30 FPS in Battery Saver mode.

### 2. GPU Hardware Video Compression
- Engine: Metal GPU accelerated image processing via `CIContext(mtlDevice:)`.
- Latency: Sub-3ms encode latency per frame.
- Color Space: Full Rec.709 sRGB color reproduction without color banding.
- Telemetry: Real-time calculation of FPS, throughput (Mbps), and encoder latency (ms).

### 3. Smart TV Protocol Controllers
- Discovery:
  - mDNS (Multicast DNS) for Google Cast devices.
  - SSDP (Simple Service Discovery Protocol) over UDP 239.255.255.250:1900 for UPnP / DLNA renderers.
- Chromecast & Google TV:
  - Protocol: CastV2 TLS connection over port 8009 with Protobuf payloads.
  - Native receiver application orchestration without third-party app requirements.
- DLNA / UPnP Media Renderers:
  - Protocol: SOAP XML control over HTTP AVTransport service (`SetAVTransportURI`, `Play`, `Pause`, `Stop`).
  - Compatible with: Samsung Tizen (2016+), LG webOS (3.0+), Sony Bravia, Roku TV, Philips, Panasonic, Xiaomi.

### 4. Zero-Client Web Receiver (`/` and `/tv`)
- Technology: Pure HTML5 Canvas 2D / WebGL rendering + Web Audio API buffer scheduling.
- Transport: WebSocket binary frame delivery + HTTP byte-range fallback.
- Client Compatibility: Any modern web browser (Mobile Safari on iPhone/iPad, Chrome on Android, Edge/Firefox on Windows/Linux, Smart TV built-in browsers).
- TV Mode (`/tv`): Designed for 10-foot viewing with high-contrast UI and remote-control friendly audio activation.

### 5. Direct 4K Video Cast
- Local Media: Supports `.mp4`, `.mov`, `.m4v`, and `.mkv` files.
- Delivery: Direct HTTP byte-range server (`206 Partial Content`) allowing Smart TVs and browsers to seek, pause, and buffer natively without CPU re-encoding.

## Quick Start & Build Instructions
```bash
git clone https://github.com/rinturajc/ezkuCasting.git
cd ezkuCasting
./Scripts/build_app.sh
# Optional: generate DMG installer
./Scripts/build_dmg.sh
# Run application
open "build/ezku.link.app"
```

## System Requirements
- Operating System: macOS 14.0 Sonoma or macOS 15.0 Sequoia
- Hardware: Mac with Apple Silicon (M1, M1 Pro/Max/Ultra, M2, M3, M4)
- Permissions: Screen & System Audio Recording (`System Settings > Privacy & Security`)
- Network: Local Wi-Fi network with client-to-client communication enabled (standard home/office Wi-Fi).

## FAQs
- Q: Do I need to install an app on my Smart TV?
  A: No. ezku.link utilizes native casting protocols (Google Cast and DLNA) already present in your Smart TV.
- Q: Can viewers on Windows or mobile devices watch?
  A: Yes. Any device on the same Wi-Fi can scan the QR code or open the local IP in their web browser.
- Q: Is any video or audio sent to the cloud?
  A: Never. ezku.link operates 100% locally on your home network.
